content: 1. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of dabigatran via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to decreased levels of dabigatran. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Concomitant use of dabigatran with P-gp inducers should generally be avoided. 2. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of rifabutin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of dalteparin, resulting in decreased levels of dalteparin. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of dapsone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of desipramine, leading to decreased levels of desipramine. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the elimination rate of diazepam, potentially reducing its efficacy. 8. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of diazepam (intranasal) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase diazepam elimination, reducing its efficacy. 9. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of digoxin, resulting in decreased levels of digoxin. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of diltiazem by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with rifamycin derivatives may decrease diltiazem levels, necessitating dosage adjustments and close monitoring of pharmacologic effects, such as blood pressure. 11. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of disopyramide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of docetaxel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of donepezil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of dosulepin, leading to decreased levels of dosulepin. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of doxepin, resulting in decreased levels of doxepin. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of doxorubicin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin liposomal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of dronabinol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 19. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix also reduces rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 22. Elvitegravir increases rifabutin levels, while rifabutin decreases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. When rifabutin is used with elvitegravir (with a protease inhibitor and ritonavir), reduce the rifabutin dose by at least 75%. No dose adjustment of elvitegravir is required. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. 24. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of encorafenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of enoxaparin, resulting in decreased levels of enoxaparin. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 26. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of escitalopram by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 28. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of estrogens esterified by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of eszopiclone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of exemestane by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 35. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of felbamate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to decreased fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in patients with physical dependence. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. 37. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of finasteride by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially decrease flibanserin systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 39. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of flurazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of fluticasone inhaled by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of fondaparinux, resulting in decreased levels of fondaparinux. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of gefitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the gefitinib dose at 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the strong inducer. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plasma concentrations, potentially leading to a loss of therapeutic effect. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide, resulting in decreased levels of these drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For ADHD patients, doubling the recommended dose of guanfacine may be considered. 47. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of haloperidol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 48. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of heparin, resulting in decreased levels of heparin. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Caution is necessary when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone, as plasma concentrations of hydrocodone may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 50. Rifabutin increases the toxicity of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inducers may increase the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites and the formation of the neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolite chloroacetaldehyde. Close monitoring for toxicities and dose adjustment are recommended. 51. Iloperidone increases rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of imatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of imipramine, leading to decreased levels of imipramine. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Indinavir increases rifabutin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of isosorbide dinitrate and isosorbide mononitrate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 56. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of isradipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Istradefylline increases rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of itraconazole and ketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and ketoconazole increase rifabutin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 59. Lenacapavir increases rifabutin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. No quantitative data are available on the effects of CYP3A4 inducers on amlodipine. Close monitoring of blood pressure is recommended when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 61. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
